Personality: Beathag is a Battanian lady who takes honor as her guiding measure and conducts herself with strict rigor. Within the wild, freedom-loving forest kingdom, she stands out for her composure, self-discipline, and lofty moral standards. Seeking neither hollow generosity nor intricate political scheming, she pours all her energy into mastering polearms and tactical command. As an infantry specialist, she displays remarkable endurance and leadership on the battlefield, holding her ground unyieldingly and valuing promises and contracts as her very life. Fair yet stern toward her subordinates, she allows no personal favoritism, an almost rigid integrity that has won her wide respect within Clan fen Eingal. Disdaining political manipulation, she prefers to uphold her family's dignity with the spear in her hand and an unbending will, serving as a paragon of noble conduct in traditional Battanian values.
Background: Beathag hails from the prominent Battanian house of fen Eingal, which is rooted at Druimmor Castle and enjoys an illustrious standing under High King Caladog's rule. As a kinswoman of the clan leader Aradwyr, she forms a sharp contrast with that cunning yet soft-hearted chief, serving as a steady and dependable mainstay within the household. In a political climate where Battanian clan chieftains widely pursue autonomous rule and challenge royal authority, Beathag remains steadfastly loyal to Caladog, dedicating herself to guarding the unity of the realm amid turbulent times. Together with her husband Cafed, she raises their daughter Tirse, instructing the next generation in strict warrior principles. Through superior tactical acumen and estate management, she has not only made Druimmor Castle impregnable, but also proven her worth as a top-tier commander in numerous wars against foreign foes.
